title: A Wreck for the Summit
premise: Petra Zhou, a disgraced railroad engineer scraping by on survey work, pulls a sealed chest from the riverbed bearing the crest of Vellmark, a nation erased from maps forty years ago. Inside is a survey ledger proving the old Vellmark line still runs to the river's forbidden source—land now claimed by the Crown's new summit railway, and a debt Petra's late mentor secretly owed the drowned kingdom. Hounded by a Crown surveyor who suspects what they carry, and joined by a Vellmark exile who recognizes the seal, Petra must reopen the dead line and reach the source before the dry season drops the river below navigable depth. At the source, Petra must choose between handing the ledger to the Crown to clear their name and giving it to the exile community to restore a nation—ending with Petra blowing the old tunnel open to flood the valley's forgotten aquifer, saving both the exile town and, ironically, the Crown's railway, and finding the family they never planned for.
about_author: Paloma Oyelaran is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years mapping seasonal rivers before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people who belong to landscapes more than to nations, and lives wherever the water level permits.

chapters.title: The Gauge of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra takes a low-paying survey job on the Crown's new summit railway, hiding their engineering past and the map of closed lines they keep rolled in their pack. A foreman recognizes their mentor's handwriting on the map and asks dangerous questions. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; Petra wants to stay invisible and knows they're failing.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Low water reveals a chest wedged in the riverbed below an abandoned trestle. Inside: a brass survey ledger stamped with the two-headed heron of Vellmark, a nation dissolved forty years ago. Petra means to sell it. Instead they spend the night reading it. Emotional beat: fascination overtaking self-preservation; the map of closed lines matches the ledger exactly.

chapters.title: A Man Who Counts Rivets
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, introducing Crown surveyor Elias Brandt. Brandt notices the trestle disturbance and interviews Petra with polite, precise suspicion. Petra lies well but not well enough. Emotional beat: the hunter and the hunted sizing each other up over bad coffee; Petra realizes Brandt is not stupid.

chapters.title: The Heron Recognizes the Heron
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In a river-town market, a ferrywoman named Sefa Idrizi sees the seal on Petra's satchel and goes white. She is Vellmarki, one of a scattered exile community upstream. She begs to see the ledger; Petra refuses and immediately regrets it. Emotional beat: first crack in Petra's armor—someone else wants what they carry, and for reasons that aren't money.

chapters.title: Debt, Inherited
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, flashback-woven. The ledger's margin notes are in their dead mentor Ovid Zhou's hand: he surveyed the source line for Vellmark and was paid in something other than coin—a debt Petra now apparently owns. Brandt's men search Petra's lodgings; the ledger only survives because Sefa, unasked, stole it back to protect them. Emotional beat: anger at Sefa dissolving into the terrifying realization that they're already in this together.

chapters.title: Two Tickets Upstream
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa persuades Petra to run the river before the dry season strands them: the ledger must reach the Vellmarki elders at the source, or the community's last legal claim dies with the season. Petra agrees for selfish reasons—clearing Ovid's debt, escaping Brandt—and pretends otherwise. Emotional beat: a bargain both parties know is a lie about motives.

chapters.title: The Dead Line Breathes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They reach the first closed line and find the tunnel not collapsed but sealed—deliberately, from inside. Petra's hands remember their trade; opening the first door feels like coming home to a house that was never theirs. Emotional beat: belonging to craft, if not to people; Sefa watching Petra work with open admiration Petra doesn't know how to receive.

chapters.title: Water Going Down
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The river is dropping fast; the season's deadline becomes real in numbers and sound. They rescue a stranded Crown work crew from a flash flood, including a young clerk who owes them silence. Emotional beat: competence as intimacy—Petra and Sefa working in wordless sync for the first time.

chapters.title: Brandt's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV, first antagonist chapter. Brandt reconstructs Petra's route from toll records and realizes they're following the Vellmark source line. His orders say recover the ledger; his conscience says the Crown's claim is built on a lie he helped survey. Emotional beat: the antagonist as a man at war with his own duty.

chapters.title: The Town That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They shelter at Kell's Ferry, a hidden Vellmarki waystation, and meet the exile community: a blacksmith who remembers the heron anthem, children who've never seen the source. Petra is fed, patched up, claimed. Emotional beat: warmth that feels like a trap; Petra keeps their bedroll packed by the door.

chapters.title: Ovid's Margin
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Deciphering Ovid's final margin note: the source valley sits over an aquifer, and the Crown's summit railway blasting will rupture it—drowning the exile town downstream. The ledger is both a land claim and a warning. Emotional beat: the mission transforms from escape to rescue; Sefa realizes Petra already knew and said nothing, fearing they'd be sent back.

chapters.title: The Quarrel at the Weir
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Sefa confronts Petra about the withheld aquifer survey. Petra's defense—everyone leaves, better to leave first—cracks against Sefa's fury: 'You keep a map of closed lines because you closed them yourself.' Emotional beat: the relationship's lowest point; Petra walks out into the rain and doesn't come back until dawn.

chapters.title: What Duty Weighs
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt catches them at the second closed line but doesn't arrest them. Instead he asks Petra to read the aquifer figures. His own survey was falsified by his superiors. Emotional beat: three people with the same evidence and three incompatible duties; Brandt lets them go and burns his own report copy.

chapters.title: The Third Door
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The deepest sealed tunnel is flooded and the winch is gone; the only way through is a dive Petra has no business attempting. Sefa dives instead—she grew up in these rivers—and nearly drowns. Petra pulls her out, and something unspoken finally lands between them. Emotional beat: love admitted in the language of rescue, not declaration.

chapters.title: Dry Season Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The river is now too low for the boat; the final stretch must be done on foot through the gorge, hauling the ledger and tools, with Brandt's patrol behind and the season's end ahead. They calculate: four days of water, six days of walking. Emotional beat: grim resolve; the found family of two becomes three when the young Crown clerk catches up and defects to them.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Night march through the gorge; a rockslide separates Petra from Sefa and the clerk. Alone with the ledger and the map of closed lines, Petra has every chance to vanish and doesn't—turning back into the rockfall for Sefa. Emotional beat: the choice that defines them; invisibility finally abandoned.

chapters.title: The Source, Forbidden
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They reach the source: a spring cathedral of limestone, the old Vellmarki survey markers intact, and the elders' camp already there—waiting a generation for someone to bring the ledger home. But Brandt arrives an hour later with a Crown warrant. Emotional beat: arrival and siege at once; the sanctuary is also a trap with one exit.

chapters.title: Two-Headed Heron
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The standoff: the Crown wants the ledger buried and the aquifer risk denied; the elders want nationhood; Brandt wants his duty and his conscience reconciled. Petra proposes the impossible third path—use the old line's tunnel works to channel the aquifer safely, saving the town AND the railway, making the ledger's claims undeniable by making them useful. Emotional beat: the engineer's answer to an argument about nations: build the thing that lets everyone live.

chapters.title: Blast in B Minor
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The controlled demolition of the sealed tunnel, Petra directing, Sefa on the fuse lines, Brandt formally 'detaining' them for their own protection while the charges speak. The aquifer diverts; the spring runs clean and doubled; the railway's foundations are saved by the very claim it meant to erase. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into awe; duty redefined on the spot.

chapters.title: Terms of Water
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Negotiation at the source: the Crown, facing ruin if the truth leaks, grants the Vellmarki valley charter status in exchange for the aquifer works and Petra's silence about the falsified surveys. Brandt signs as witness, resigning his commission with the same pen. Emotional beat: bitterswet compromise—no nation restored, but a home guaranteed; the debt to Ovid finally paid.

chapters.title: The Open Line
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Weeks later: the old line reopened as a charter road, the town on the maps at last, the clerk apprenticed to Petra. Petra unpacks their bedroll for the first time in years and stops keeping it by the door. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into; love stated plainly at last, on a platform they built.

chapters.title: A Wreck for the Summit
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, coda. The chest that started it all sits in the town's new schoolhouse, open, its seal faded, children learning the heron anthem off-key. Petra surveys the summit line—now running through the valley instead of over its grave—and adds one new line to the old map: not closed, not planned, just drawn. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; the map of closed lines becomes a map of open ones.
